verdict.rationale: Skyvern's product page states that generated Playwright code is cached after the first run and that repeat runs skip the LLM entirely. It claims this makes runs faster, cheaper and fully deterministic, which covers every element of the story. The support rests on a single marketing claim, with no in-depth developer documentation and no hands-on corroboration. Missing for 10: developer docs on enabling and controlling the code cache (invalidation, fallback when the page changes), independent or hands-on verification of the speed, cost and determinism claims.

support.subject: As a developer, I can cache resolved actions or generated code so repeat runs replay deterministically at lower cost and latency than re-prompting the LLM

citations.quote: Generated Playwright code is cached after the first run. Repeat runs skip the LLM entirely — 3–5× faster, up to 70% cheaper, fully deterministic.
